text: The X5 slice consumes three things that no metadata row carries and they are read as non-blocking and built against their fakes: the rwb-case case read and the pause, resume and route announcement, on a published case contract whose operation name is left as the placeholder; the LOV-DEVIATION, LOV-RAISED-BY and LOV-DEV-OUTCOME values on the reference data of rwb-case through the platform client library (DP-07 is not in the pattern set); and the platform outbox behind the two published events (DP-09 is not in the pattern set either). The metadata row keeps the plan's list exactly, with Contract, Integration and External dependencies None, and the two platform contracts of the pattern set (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) stay in the build list. Both slices trace to FEAT-DVF-05 and carry no requirement identifier, and the requirement column of both stories and of both fragments stays empty.
why: The plan's dependency rows for this key name no contract, integration or external dependency while the story must reach the case of record, three list codes and the event platform, and the requirement identifier exists in no source; inventing a C or H row would change the build sequence, calling a table directly would break DP-01 and DP-05, and writing a requirement identifier by pattern would create a reference no owner approved.

text: The claim deadline that R-DEV-05's action names and the 10-working-day service level of R-DEV-20 are versioned reference rows, never code, and their values are carried as the placeholder. The deadline is held as a durable timer of DeviationWorkflow with the reference row as its source, and the SLA timer is a second durable timer of the same workflow.
why: The Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row gives the service level only as "deadline driven" and no source in the fill order gives a number; writing one would be a business value with no owner, and holding the deadline as a timer of this workflow is the only place the story can hold a clock, because the case timer is the case of record's.

text: The Legal handler route of R-DEV-05 is a versioned reference row from deviation code to handler role, and the handler is stored as handler_user_id on the deviation. Both operations declare Case record right U, as the legacy permission block gives it, and the question of whether RW-LEGAL may write, which FSD S8 A2.14.3.3 and TSD S8 T6.1 answer differently, is left to rwb-access: this run neither widens the role nor narrows the operation.
why: The rule names "Legal" and the row stores a handler, but no source gives the role code, the queue or the assignment target, and the right of the primary actor differs between the FSD and the TSD; choosing either one quietly would change an access control and a business route without an owner.

text: DeviationRaised (EV-06) and DeviationCleared (EV-07) are published as the event catalogue assigns them, through the platform outbox and inbox library, although DP-09 is not in this key's pattern set and RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is therefore not in the metadata. The two payloads are exactly the three fields each catalogue row gives, in the CloudEvents envelope of the naming rule.
why: The events are assigned to this service by the event catalogue and the timers and communications that consume them need the pause and the resume, so omitting them would leave the stage clock with no signal; declaring an outbox pattern that the plan does not give the key would change the pattern list and the dependency row, so both are carried here instead.

text: The filing fact BANKRUPTCY_FILED and the answers of the case announcement reach this service as events of rwb-case on rwb.case.events.v1, consumed once through an inbox keyed on the CloudEvents id, because Architecture v5 slide 13 gives rwb-deviation no REST edge to rwb-litigation, rwb-decision or rwb-comms and only an E to rwb-case. why: The filing is rwb-litigation's act and the case is rwb-case's, so the fact has to travel through an owner both services already talk to; a direct call to S4 would add a cross-service read that the matrix does not give, and reading the legal action table would break DP-01.
